# What this is and who it is for

::: {.callout-note}
Revised with assistance from OpenAI Codex/GPT-6. Earlier skeleton drafted by Claude Code/Fable 5.1. This summary remains unfinished.
:::

This study describes words understood, spoken and signed by children with Down syndrome. It combines parent-reported checklist counts from research studies and uses statistical models to describe age-related patterns and differences between children. This summary is for families and practitioners who want context for vocabulary records.

The models use a reference of `{python} N_WORDS` items. The studies used different word lists, languages and response options. A common reference scale does not mean that each checklist asked about the same words.

Parents reported the words their children understood, said or signed. The families took part in research projects and were not selected as a random sample of all children with Down syndrome. Predictions therefore describe possible counts under the model for the contributing research pool.

This summary describes the fitted output recorded as `{python} generated_from()`.
